title: Paid help with veterans' claims
dek: A company that charges veterans for help with disability claims, the veterans groups that give that help for free, and the bills that would decide between them. None has had a vote.
why: Bills that would decide whether companies may charge veterans for help with claims, where the company and the veterans groups that give that help for free both file their own lobbying reports, so the two can be set side by side.

focus: VETERANS GUARDIAN VA CLAIM CONSULTING LLC
others: VETERANS OF FOREIGN WARS OF THE UNITED STATES
IRAQ AND AFGHANISTAN VETERANS OF AMERICA, INC.

facts.text: The Veterans Benefits, Health Care, and Information Technology Act of 2006 repeals the criminal penalty for charging prohibited fees for help with a VA claim. Charging without accreditation stays against the law, with no criminal penalty.

Reps. Chris Pappas, Brian Fitzpatrick and Jeff Van Drew reintroduce the GUARD VA Benefits Act (H.R. 1732), which would reinstate criminal penalties for unaccredited representatives who charge unauthorized fees for help with a VA disability claim. DAV and the VFW back it.
Rep. Jack Bergman introduces the PLUS for Veterans Act (H.R. 1656), which would let companies like Veterans Guardian become accredited and charge capped fees.
The American Legion tells Congress it supports H.R. 1732 and opposes H.R. 1656. The Military Officers Association also backs the GUARD Act.

source.title: The American Legion, statement for the record

facts.text: H.R. 1732 is referred to the Veterans' Affairs Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs.
The full House Veterans' Affairs Committee holds a legislative hearing that includes H.R. 1732. It has not voted on the bill.

source.title: House Veterans' Affairs Committee, hearing notice, Mar. 18, 2026

facts.text: In a class action, the federal district court for the Middle District of North Carolina finds the evidence undisputed that Veterans Guardian acted as an unaccredited agent. The VA had sent the company cease-and-desist letters in 2019 and 2024. The company disputes this and says its work is consulting, not representation.

Reps. Janelle Bynum, Chris Pappas, Don Bacon and Mike Lawler introduce the SAFEGUARD Veterans Act (H.R. 9105), and Sen. Richard Blumenthal a Senate companion (S. 4646), to restore criminal penalties for unaccredited representatives who charge veterans.

source.title: American Legion Department of California, June 9, 2026

facts.text: In the same case, the court finds Veterans Guardian committed unfair trade practices under North Carolina law during much of the class period.

not_yet: Contributions by the company's executives as individuals (in FEC records, not lobbying reports) and lobbying in state legislatures are not on this page.

TRAJECTOR MEDICAL.why: a for-profit company (Trajector, Inc.) that testified before House Veterans' Affairs subcommittees as an unaccredited claims preparation company (CCK Law's summary of the hearing: cck-law.com). Its description mentions veterans, which the word rules read as advocacy.
